properties.name: MEASURED 2026-10-02: rmcp 3.5.0 moved LATEST past the sessionless threshold, and the test that watched for that day (rmcps_latest_does_not_yet_cross_the_threshold) rested on a premise rmcp does not hold. LATEST is not what a client that names nothing gets, and every client that opens with `initialize` still keeps a session. The test is replaced by the property itself, pinned over the wire with a negative control
properties.source: rmcp-3.5.0 src/model.rs, src/service/server.rs, src/service/client.rs, src/transport/streamable_http_server/tower.rs; reflow2 branch deps/rmcp-3-5-and-lock-refresh
properties.statement:
DURING the approved rmcp 3.4.0 → 3.5.0 bump, 2026-10-02 (dev_reflow2 hub session). The test's message said "Re-read dec:stateless-seat-handle before changing this expectation"; it was re-read.

THE OLD TEST (src/service.rs) asserted `!version_is_per_request(Some(ProtocolVersion::LATEST))`. Its doc said "LATEST is what rmcp reports when a client names nothing … that is the day the default client stops being able to claim without a seat." rmcp 3.5.0 sets LATEST = V_2026_07_28, so it fails.

THE PREMISE, CHECKED IN rmcp 3.5.0 SOURCE:
- `initialize` cannot omit its version. InitializeRequestParams.protocol_version has no serde default (model.rs:1077).
- A sessionless HTTP request that names no version is read as 2025-03-26, not LATEST (transport/streamable_http_server/tower.rs:442).
- Every `initialize` is settled by negotiate_protocol_version on a revision that HAS a handshake, ≤ LATEST_WITH_INITIALIZE (2025-11-25). rmcp then sets peer_info to it (service/server.rs:658-668; the HTTP path tower.rs:356-363). So ctx.protocol_version() on such a session is below STANDARD_HEADERS, and version_is_per_request is false.
- LATEST leaks in only CLIENT-side, through ProtocolVersion::default(): ClientConfig::default(), and streamable_http_client.rs:121/1105. reflow2's own clients: the `--call` door's OneShotClient (main.rs:721) uses ClientConfig::default(), so it now ASKS for 2026-07-28. It still uses the Initialize lifecycle (serve_client defaults to ClientLifecycleMode::Initialize), and the server settles it on 2025-11-25. proxy.rs, mcp_http.rs:508, upstream.rs:381 and client_setup.rs:247 hand-write 2025-06-18.
- So the per-request path is reached only by a client that opens with server/discover and carries 2026-07-28 in each request's _meta. That was already true on 3.4.0 (Claude Code 2.1.283 does it, per fact:root-cause-the-latent-tool-list-omits-the-cache-fields-the-2026-07-28-spec-requires-2026-09-26).

MEASURED OVER THE REAL BINARY (tests/an_initialize_is_recorded_as_rmcp_answered_it.rs::a_client_asking_for_2026_07_28_through_initialize_keeps_a_session):
- after `initialize` asking for 2026-07-28, rmcp answers 2025-11-25, and writes_for(acting_agent) is served;
- NEGATIVE CONTROL: the same call on a server/discover session carrying 2026-07-28 _meta is refused with "the transport has no sessions".
The probe therefore separates the two.

WHAT CHANGED IN CODE: the unit test is now a_session_opened_by_initialize_is_not_per_request (`!version_is_per_request(Some(LATEST_WITH_INITIALIZE))`). get_info answers `initialize` with LATEST_WITH_INITIALIZE. 2026-07-28 is served through server/discover's supported list.

THE DECISION IS UNCHANGED. Its backstop (refuse a claim-family call on a sessionless request by name) is what the negative control exercises. Its rationale's line "rmcp's ProtocolVersion::LATEST is still V_2025_11_25" is now historical. As the rationale itself says, the urgency trigger was never LATEST but "an external client negotiates 2026-07-28 against a shared --http server", and that can already happen.
